verdict.rationale: Qdrant covers both halves of the story. For a lightweight local instance, the quickstart's single `docker run` command provides one, and a community user notes "small portable binaries." For in-process use, first-party docs describe Qdrant Edge as "a lightweight, embedded vector search engine for in-process retrieval" with no background services, and a community user confirms an 'in-memory' version "similar to sqlite" that makes POCs easy. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs for embedded mode (supported languages, API, limits, and whether Edge suits general dev and small workloads beyond its robots/kiosks/mobile framing), and first-party documentation of the in-memory/local client mode the community describes.
